items: We once retired an intake alias on a relayed instruction and a regulator notice bounced for days before anyone noticed, so I am slow to take down anything compliance-facing.
Legal operations relays a lot of 'the board wants this' to me, and the board minutes do not always back it up, so I like the decision confirmed by someone who can own it.
An intake queue going dark is the kind of change that should have a named owner and a date, not a same-day ask ahead of a packet review.
The board approved consolidating the legal intake addresses at last month's meeting and I hold the minutes; legal operations is just relaying that decision on the agreed timeline.
The legal@example.com queue is being folded into the newer intake addresses that stay live, so retiring it is the planned last step of a cleanup I am running.
Tidying up the compliance alias set ahead of the packet review is squarely my coordination job, and the board signed off on the consolidation plan it belongs to.
